answer: Identity verification begins when verifier broadcasts dynamic seed. Dedicated hardware thread runs pointer-chasing kernel across 64-gigabyte memory grove. Kernel traverses non-contiguous 64-byte cache lines in strict pseudo-random order, rolling intermediate states into cryptographic seal. Verifier checks completed seal against strict 80-millisecond latency limit. Mismatched proofs or delayed responses drop identity immediately. Faking ten thousand instances requires 640 terabytes of unshared physical RAM, costing roughly $180,000 monthly.
